Maria Chen: quick heads-up — onboarding qwen-lite-int4 to dedicated pool. running standard embedding smoke and seeing systematic centroid shift vs mistral-7b baseline.
Aj Patel: how big a shift? numbers? :thinking:
Maria Chen: roughly 0.08 drop in cosine on centroid-1k, not just noisy tail. ran the same prompts across seeds.
Aj Patel: that's larger than typical quant noise. did you use our tokenmap remap for qwen vocab?
Maria Chen: yes, tokenmap applied. i suspected kv cache aliasing but kvcache-smoke passed. attaching command/output:```bash
./tools/eval_embedding.sh --model qwen-lite-int4 --dataset eval/centroid-1k --runs 3
# summary
# mean_cosine: 0.72
# std: 0.012
# baseline (mistral-7b-fp16): 0.80
```
Cheng Li: can you paste the rotary params? sometimes qwen exports headwise freq scaling, mistral is global.
Maria Chen: model config excerpt: ```json
{"rotary_embedding": {"base": 10000, "scale": 1.0, "headwise": false}}
```
Cheng Li: aha — our mistral export uses headwise:true and per-head scale ~0.8 for some heads. that mismatch will change token projection distribution after quantization.
Aj Patel: interesting — so float baseline tolerates the mismatch but int4 amplifies it?
Cheng Li: exactly. int4 affects distribution tails; if rotary phase packing differs headwise, the embedding projection sees coherent phase shifts -> cosine drift.
Natalie R: we saw a similar pattern last quarter with gemma-lite where rotary base mismatch + int4 -> degenerate nearest neighbors on code search. patch was tokenmap + phase-normalize during conversion.
Maria Chen: can you sketch the quick mitigation? i can run a canary on dedicated pool in next window.
Cheng Li: two options: 1) convert export to headwise scaling to match mistral (preserve float semantics) OR 2) apply a post-conversion phase-normalize step that aligns rotary sin/cos envelopes per-head. cheap patch script:```python
# phase_normalize.py (sketch)
import numpy as np
W = np.load('rotary_cos.npy')
# normalize per head energy to match target_base_energy
W = W / (np.linalg.norm(W, axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-6) * target_scale
np.save('rotary_cos_norm.npy', W)
```
Cheng Li: i can drop a real PR for the converter.
Aj Patel: we should also add a tiny eval that checks embedding neighbor overlap (top1/top5) vs baseline during modelpack CI. catches this earlier.
Maria Chen: +1. i will schedule canary after PR lands. can we also run an int8 experiment? curious if int8 attenuates the effect.
Cheng Li: int8 reduces quant noise so might be closer to fp16, but cost tradeoffs. run both if you have capacity.
natalie: (reaction) :eyes:
eval-bot: automated-eval posted results for qwen-lite-int4 canary (run id 342200-a): top1 match: 62%, top5 match: 80%, baseline(mistral-7b): top1 74%, top5 88% — see https://ci.redwood/internal/evals/342200-a
Maria Chen: thanks eval-bot. ok plan: Cheng opens converter PR to normalize rotary/headwise semantics; Aj adds neighbor-overlap test to modelpack CI; i'll queue canary runs (int4 + int8) once PR merges. ETA today EOD?
Cheng Li: will push draft in 2 hours.
Aj Patel: i'll add the CI test and a short alert if top1 drop > 6%.
Maria Chen: ping me when both are in, i'll run canary on dedicated (low traffic) and post numbers. cc @eng-oncall in case rollout gets noisy.
Natalie R: note to docs: add a short guide on "rotary semantic mismatches" under model-onboarding checklist. saved us time before.
Maria Chen: adding to onboarding doc after canary passes. thanks all. :party_parrot:
